answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a kernel before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a challenge proves the agent duplicated credentials or colluded. A sparrow can still join, but creating a grove of fake accounts now ties up capital in every one and risks losing it; the attacker's cost rises with the number of identities, rather than with the cheap act of generating names. This raises the price of a sybil attack without claiming to make identities impossible to forge.
